title_en: EASA orders emergency checks of Airbus H160 cockpit windows
title_zh: EASA下令对空客H160驾驶舱窗户进行紧急检查
summary: Europe’s aviation safety regulator has ordered emergency inspections of Airbus H160-B helicopters after an assembly-line check revealed that… The post EASA orders emergency checks of Airbus H160 cockpit windows appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 装配线检查显示……欧洲航空安全监管机构已下令对空客 H160-B 直升机进行紧急检查。
body_en: Europe’s aviation safety regulator has ordered emergency inspections of Airbus H160-B helicopters after an assembly-line check revealed that cockpit escape windows could come loose and detach in flight.
The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) issued the directive on November 25, 2026. It took effect on November 27.

The directive covers all H160-B serial numbers. Helicopters fitted with the affected pilot or copilot windows must be inspected within 10 flight hours of the effective date. If an inspection finds a problem, operators must correct it before flying the helicopter again.
Airbus Helicopters issued an emergency service bulletin on November 24 with instructions for checking the window installation.

The issue surfaced during a test after the windows had been installed on the assembly line. A red warning flag on the cockpit window’s lock indicator remained visible. A subsequent investigation found that when the flag remained even partly visible, the window could unlock and detach in flight.
EASA said a detached window could damage the helicopter or injure people on the ground.
The H160 entered US service in 2024 with PHI Aviation, which uses the helicopter for offshore energy operations.
EASA did not specify how many helicopters have the affected windows.

body_zh: 欧洲航空安全监管机构已下令对空客 H160-B 直升机进行紧急检查，此前装配线检查显示驾驶舱逃生窗可能在飞行中松动和脱落。
欧盟航空安全局（EASA）于2026年11月25日发布该指令，并于11月27日生效。
该指令涵盖所有 H160-B 序列号。装有受影响的飞行员或副驾驶窗户的直升机必须在生效日期后 10 个飞行小时内进行检查。如果检查发现问题，操作员必须在再次驾驶直升机之前进行纠正。
空中客车直升机公司于 11 月 24 日发布了紧急服务公告，其中包含检查窗户安装的说明。
该问题是在窗户安装到装配线上后进行的测试中出现的。驾驶舱窗户锁定指示器上的红色警告旗仍然可见。随后的调查发现，当旗帜甚至部分可见时，窗户可能会在飞行中解锁和分离。
欧洲航空安全局表示，脱落的窗户可能会损坏直升机或伤害地面人员。
H160 于 2024 年在 PHI Aviation 进入美国服役，该公司使用该直升机进行海上能源作业。
欧洲航空安全局没有具体说明有多少架直升机的窗户受到影响。

title_en: AirAsia Philippines cuts jobs, faces strike as AirAsia Group delays staff salaries
title_zh: 菲律宾亚航集团推迟员工工资，裁员并面临罢工
summary: AirAsia Philippines is to cut jobs and scale back routes and flight frequencies, with high jet fuel prices… The post AirAsia Philippines cuts jobs, faces strike as AirAsia Group delays staff salaries appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 菲律宾亚航将裁员并缩减航线和航班频率，航空燃油价格高企……菲律宾亚航裁员后，FA
body_en: AirAsia Philippines is to cut jobs and scale back routes and flight frequencies, with high jet fuel prices and a weak peso driving up its operating costs. Local media has reported that about 90 captains and first officers have been told their employment will end on December 31, 2026.

“AirAsia Philippines has made the very difficult decision to reduce our workforce. Sustained pressure from elevated jet fuel prices and unfavorable exchange rates has significantly increased our operating costs,” President and General Manager Anna Victoria Lu said in a statement on November 26, 2026.

“In response, we had to carefully evaluate and optimize our routes and flight frequencies to keep operations sustainable, which have a significant effect on our manpower requirements,” Lu added. “These tough adjustments are being made to ensure the long-term stability of the airline, in the best interest of our passengers and our dearest Allstars.”

The airline did not say how many employees were affected or which routes and flights will be cut, although local media, citing the pilots’ union, has reported that about 90 pilots have received retrenchment notices.

Lu stressed that the company would support those who are leaving. “We deeply recognize the impact this has on our colleagues and their families, and we are committed to supporting them with care and transparency through this transition,” she said.

The Philippine Star reported that AirAsia Philippines has been one of the country’s hardest-hit carriers, closing some flights to save costs as jet fuel crossed USD 200 per barrel. Like other local airlines, it earns most of its revenue in pesos but pays most of its expenses in US dollars, so the peso’s weakness has added to the strain.

On November 27, 2026, the airline declared that its flights would operate as scheduled. “AirAsia Philippines remains fully operational and committed to serving the Philippine market,” Lu said. “We want to assure our passengers that the announced workforce adjustment will not affect their flight, booking, or other services.”
Pilots’ union files strike notice as labor department steps in

The layoffs have spawned a labor dispute. According to the Manila Standard and Bilyonaryo, the AirAsia Philippines Pilots Union (APPU) filed a petition for a certification election on September 4 so that pilots could choose their collective bargaining representative. The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) granted the petition on November 19, and the union received the order on November 25.

That same week, management announced the workforce reduction at a meeting with pilots, the union said. Around 90 pilots then lost access to their crew schedules and were called to individual meetings with management between November 25 and 27. Those who attended on November 25 received retrenchment notices effective December 31, 2026.

APPU President Oscar Joseph Ramos Jr. told local media that the retrenchment had been rushed, with too little consultation and outstanding issues left unaddressed. The Philippine Star reported that the union had sought to represent close to 200 pilots, which implies that nearly half of them will be gone by the end of the year.
The Trade Union Congress of the Philippines (TUCP) questioned the timing, called the move ‘union busting’ and asked lawmakers to investigate.

APPU filed a notice of strike at the DOLE main office in Manila on November 26. Labor Secretary Francis Tolentino said the agency had formed a task force and convened the National Conciliation and Mediation Board to bring both sides together on November 27. He told local reporters the dispute was a top priority because a strike could disrupt flights ahead of the year-end holidays, and that he would oversee the talks himself.
Group defers salaries as losses and fuel costs mount
The cuts in the Philippines come as the wider group tightens its finances.
On November 27, 2026, Reuters reported that AirAsia had informed its Malaysia-based employees that their salaries would be paid at the end of each month from November through March 2027.

According to an internal email sent by Chief People Officer Muhammad Khurram Zia, the change is a temporary operational adjustment. AirAsia had previously paid salaries earlier, during the second half of each month, one person familiar with the matter told the news agency.

AirAsia, which employs about 26,000 people, mostly in Asia, reported its third consecutive quarterly loss on November 23, 2026, although the loss was narrower than in the previous quarter. Its cash and bank balances stood at MYR 905 million (USD 220 million) as of September 30, down 5% from the end of June.

To conserve cash, the airline has suspended unviable routes and returned 25 aircraft to lessors, with more expected to leave the fleet during 2027. A creditor restructuring is also underway, as part of a plan to reset the business before rebuilding in 2028.

Group CEO Bo Lingam, the third-quarter results suggested the worst was over, but warned that fuel costs would rise further in the fourth quarter. The company’s shares have fallen more than 70% this year.
body_zh: 由于航空燃油价格高涨和比索疲软推高了其运营成本，菲律宾亚航将裁员并缩减航线和航班频率。当地媒体报道称，约 90 名船长和副驾驶已被告知他们的雇佣关系将于 2026 年 12 月 31 日结束。
“菲律宾亚航做出了裁员的非常艰难的决定。航油价格上涨和不利汇率带来的持续压力显着增加了我们的运营成本，”总裁兼总经理 Anna Victoria Lu 在 2026 年 11 月 26 日的一份声明中表示。
“为此，我们必须仔细评估和优化我们的航线和航班频率，以保持运营可持续，这对我们的人力需求产生重大影响，”卢补充道。 “做出这些艰难的调整是为了确保航空公司的长期稳定，符合我们的乘客和我们最亲爱的全明星的最佳利益。”
该航空公司没有透露有多少员工受到影响，也没有透露哪些航线和航班将被削减，但当地媒体援引飞行员工会的报道称，约有 90 名飞行员已收到裁员通知。
卢强调，公司将支持那些离开的人。她说：“我们深刻认识到这对我们的同事及其家人产生的影响，我们致力于在这一过渡期间以谨慎和透明的方式支持他们。”
据《菲律宾星报》报道，菲律宾亚航是该国受打击最严重的航空公司之一，由于航油价格突破每桶 200 美元，该航空公司关闭了部分航班以节省成本。与其他当地航空公司一样，它的大部分收入以比索赚取，但大部分费用以美元支付，因此比索的疲软加剧了压力。
2026年11月27日，该航空公司宣布其航班将按计划运营。陆说：“菲律宾亚航仍全面运营，并致力于服务菲律宾市场。” “我们希望向乘客保证，宣布的劳动力调整不会影响他们的航班、预订或其他服务。”
劳工部介入，飞行员工会发出罢工通知
裁员引发了劳资纠纷。据《马尼拉标准报》和《Bilyonaryo》报道，亚航菲律宾飞行员工会（APPU）于9月4日提交了一份认证选举请愿书，以便飞行员可以选择他们的集体谈判代表。劳工和就业部 (DOLE) 于 11 月 19 日批准了请愿书，工会于 11 月 25 日收到了命令。
工会表示，同一周，管理层在与飞行员的会议上宣布裁员。随后，大约 90 名飞行员失去了机组人员的时间表，并被要求在 11 月 25 日至 27 日期间与管理层举行单独会议。11 月 25 日参加会议的飞行员收到了自 2026 年 12 月 31 日起生效的裁员通知。
APPU 主席小奥斯卡·约瑟夫·拉莫斯 (Oscar Joseph Ramos Jr.) 对当地媒体表示，此次裁员非常仓促，协商太少，而且悬而未决的问题也没有得到解决。据《菲律宾星报》报道，该工会曾寻求代表近 200 名飞行员，这意味着其中近一半将在今年年底前离职。
菲律宾工会大会（TUCP）对这一时机提出质疑，称此举是“破坏工会”，并要求立法者进行调查。
APPU 于 11 月 26 日向马尼拉劳工部总部发出罢工通知。劳工部长弗朗西斯·托伦蒂诺 (Francis Tolentino) 表示，该机构已成立一个特别工作组，并于 11 月 27 日召集全国和解与调解委员会，将双方召集在一起。他告诉当地记者，这场争端是当务之急，因为罢工可​​能会在年底假期前扰乱航班，他将亲自监督谈判。
由于亏损和燃料成本上升，集团推迟发薪
菲律宾的裁员是在整个集团收紧财政之际进行的。
2026 年 11 月 27 日，路透社报道称，亚航已通知其马来西亚员工，从 11 月到 2027 年 3 月，他们的工资将在每月月底发放。
根据首席人事官穆罕默德·胡拉姆·齐亚（Muhammad Khurram Zia）发送的内部电子邮件，这一变化是临时的运营调整。一位知情人士告诉该通讯社，亚航此前曾在每个月的下半月早些时候支付工资。
亚洲航空拥有约 26,000 名员工，大部分位于亚洲，该公司于 2026 年 11 月 23 日公布连续第三个季度亏损，不过亏损幅度较上一季度有所收窄。截至 9 月 30 日，其现金和银行余额为 9.05 亿马来西亚林吉特（2.2 亿美元），比 6 月底下降 5%。
为了节省现金，该航空公司已暂停不可行的航线，并将 25 架飞机归还给出租人，预计更多飞机将在 2027 年离开机队。债权人重组也在进行中，作为 2028 年重建之前重置业务计划的一部分。
集团首席执行官Bo Lingam表示，第三季度业绩表明最糟糕的时期已经过去，但警告称第四季度燃料成本将进一步上升。今年以来，该公司股价已下跌逾70%。

title_en: Air New Zealand Launches New 7-Hour Nonstop Route In 3 Days: See Map Now
title_zh: 新西兰航空推出三天 7 小时直飞新航线：立即查看地图
summary: New three weekly services reconnect South Island travelers to Western Australia without detours through major hubs.
summary_zh: 每周三班的新服务将南岛旅客重新连接至西澳大利亚，无需绕道主要枢纽。
body_en: Journalist – Aaron is an aviation and travel journalist with 14 years of experience in the travel and tourism industry. His background spans airport operations, aviation infrastructure, and travel consulting, having worked with global organizations across New Zealand, Europe, and North America.

Combining industry expertise with firsthand travel experience across more than 52 countries and five continents, Aaron covers airlines, airports, aviation policy, and the wider travel sector. He is based in Canterbury, New Zealand.
His work has been published in Simple Flying and featured by MSN, SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel, EIN News, Pakistan Defence, and Climate Depot.

Star Alliance member Air New Zealand is gearing up to commence its newest long-haul service, as the airline adds Christchurch (CHC) to Perth (PER) from November 30. This will be the first time the airline has operated the city pair since it terminated the nonstop service from New Zealand's South Island in 2019.

The flights are set to run seasonally, three times a week, providing another alternative for travelers looking to experience Australia's West Coast. Air New Zealand will face competition on the route, as Jetstar also operates a seasonal service.
Christchurch To Perth Takes Flight From November 30

The airline's decision to resume services to Perth came in the same announcement ​​​​​ as the carrier added Singapore (SIN) and Tokyo Narita (NRT) from the Garden City . Christchurch is the second largest city in the South Pacific nation, and its airport is the only one in the South Island equipped for widebody aircraft.

Air New Zealand will resume the service to Perth on November 30, and operate the flight up to three times a week through until May 7. These flights will complement the airline's existing year-round service from Auckland (AKL).

These new flights will add up to an additional 37,000 seats across the Southern Hemisphere summer season, and are a welcome addition to the Southern airports expansion, off the back of a successful season of short-haul seasonal flights to Rarotonga (RAR). The flights to Perth will follow the schedule detailed in the table above.
New Flights Between Christchurch & Perth Capture Strong Travel Demand

The resumption of services to Perth from Christchurch will cater to strong travel demand that otherwise has seen travelers forced to connect via other airports, including Auckland, Brisbane, Melbourne or Sydney. As already mentioned, Jetstar , the low-cost subsidiary of the Qantas Group, commenced its own seasonal service from Perth to Christchurch with its Airbus A321LR narrowbody twinjets.

These services are expected to run through until late March. Air New Zealand's return to the city pair marks the only widebody and aircraft with premium cabins serving the route. Jetstar's schedule is detailed in the table below.

Air New Zealand has an extensive domestic and trans-Tasman network from Christchurch, and the new service will be popular with both leisure and business travelers. Those visiting the South Island can now transit via Christchurch Airport from other airports across the island, without the need to travel via another major hub.
Air New Zealand Long-Haul Goes Year Round From Christchurch

With Air New Zealand having commenced its nonstop services from Christchurch to Singapore on October 28 , this marked the airline's resumption of the route since it was suspended in February 2020. On the day of the first flight this year, the carrier announced that it would actually expand its schedule to year-round.

This complements the existing daily Singapore Airlines service to Christchurch, on which it partners through a joint venture . Services from Christchurch to Tokyo Narita also take flight on November 28 , providing nonstop services to the Japanese capital through until late May. Air New Zealand previously operated nonstop flights between the two cities up until 2015.

While not operated with long-haul aircraft, Air New Zealand also quietly resumed nonstop services from Christchurch to Adelaide (ADL) in October. This route is served twice weekly onboard the carrier's Airbus A320 or A321neo, and will continue through to the end of March.
body_zh: 记者 – Aaron 是一名航空和旅行记者，在旅行和旅游业拥有 14 年的经验。他的背景涵盖机场运营、航空基础设施和旅游咨询，曾与新西兰、欧洲和北美的全球组织合作。
Aaron 将行业专业知识与五大洲超过 52 个国家/地区的第一手旅行经验相结合，涵盖航空公司、机场、航空政策和更广泛的旅行领域。他居住在新西兰坎特伯雷。
他的作品发表在《Simple Flying》上，并受到 MSN、SAM CHUI Aviation & Travel、EIN News、Pakistan Defence 和 Climate Depot 的专题报道。
星空联盟成员新西兰航空正准备开始其最新的长途服务，从 11 月 30 日起，该航空公司将增加基督城 (CHC) 至珀斯 (PER) 的航班。这将是该航空公司自 2019 年终止从新西兰南岛出发的直飞航班以来首次运营这两个城市之间的航班。
这些航班按季节运营，每周 3 趟，为想要体验澳大利亚西海岸的旅客提供了另一种选择。新西兰航空将在该航线上面临竞争，因为捷星航空也运营季节性航班。
基督城飞往珀斯的航班 11 月 30 日起
该航空公司决定恢复飞往珀斯的航班​​​​​，同时该航空公司还增加了从花园城市飞往新加坡 (SIN) 和东京成田 (NRT) 的航班。基督城是南太平洋国家第二大城市，其机场是南岛唯一一个配备宽体飞机的机场。
新西兰航空将于 11 月 30 日恢复飞往珀斯的航班，并在 5 月 7 日之前每周运营该航班最多 3 班。这些航班将补充该航空公司现有的从奥克兰 (AKL) 出发的全年航班服务。
这些新航班将在整个南半球夏季增加 37,000 个座位，在飞往拉罗汤加 (RAR) 的短途季节性航班取得成功的基础上，对南部机场的扩建来说是一个受欢迎的补充。飞往珀斯的航班将遵循上表中详细的时间表。
基督城和珀斯之间的新航班满足了强劲的旅行需求
恢复从基督城飞往珀斯的航班将满足强劲的旅行需求，否则旅客将被迫通过奥克兰、布里斯班、墨尔本或悉尼等其他机场转机。如前所述，捷星航空是澳洲航空集团的低成本子公司，利用其空客 A321LR 窄体双发喷气式飞机开始了从珀斯到基督城的季节性航班服务。
这些服务预计将持续到三月下旬。新西兰航空重返城市航线标志着该航线上唯一一架拥有高级客舱的宽体飞机。捷星航空的时间表详情如下表所示。
新西兰航空拥有从基督城出发的广泛的国内和跨塔斯曼网络，新服务将受到休闲和商务旅客的欢迎。前往南岛的游客现在可以从全岛其他机场经基督城机场转机，而无需经过另一个主要枢纽。
新西兰航空全年开通从基督城出发的长途航班
新西兰航空于10月28日开通了从基督城飞往新加坡的直飞航班，这标志着该航空公司自2020年2月暂停以来，恢复了该航线。在今年首航当天，该航空公司宣布实际上将把航班计划扩展至全年。
这补充了新加坡航空现有的飞往基督城的每日航班，新加坡航空通过合资企业在该航班上进行合作。从基督城飞往东京成田的航班也于 11 月 28 日开通，提供直达日本首都的航班直至 5 月下旬。直到 2015 年，新西兰航空此前一直在这两个城市之间运营直飞航班。
尽管没有运营长途飞机，新西兰航空也在 10 月悄然恢复了从基督城飞往阿德莱德 (ADL) 的直飞航班。该航线每周由该航空公司的空客 A320 或 A321neo 运营两次，并将持续到 3 月底。

title_en: Two American Airlines 737s Collide On Taxiway At Reagan National, One Loses Winglet
title_zh: 两架美国航空 737 飞机在里根国家机场滑行道上相撞，其中一架失去了翼尖小翼
summary: The two 737s collided while lining up for departure, leaving one without a winglet and both grounded.
summary_zh: 两架 737 飞机在准备起飞时相撞，其中一架没有翼尖小翼，双双停飞。
body_en: Luke has over a decade of experience as a travel writer and aviation analyst. As a passionate traveler based across the Middle East and Asia, Luke offers strong insights into the industry. Based in South East Asia.

Two American Airlines Boeing 737-800s collided while lining up on a taxiway at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA) on Friday evening, with images of the aftermath showing one jet had its winglet torn off. Moments after the collision, a pilot told air traffic control (ATC) that the aircraft had moved " slightly over the hold short line " and had " swapped paint " with the American jet next to it.

The mishap occurred at around 5:10 PM local time near Runway 19 and involved American Flight 638 to Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport (DFW) and American Flight 2152 to Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD). It is the second time in less than 20 months that two American-branded aircraft have collided while waiting to depart from DCA, following a similar wingtip collision in April 2025.
American 737 Winglet Torn Off In Collision At DCA

Flight tracking data shows that both 737s had taxied out and were lining up waiting to enter Runway 19, with Flight 2152 lined up behind Flight 638. When the controller instructed Flight 638 to hold short of the runway, one of its pilots reported that they had collided with a fellow American 737, before stating that they were unsure whether the two aircraft were still attached.

A pilot onboard Flight 2152 then confirmed, " Oh yeah, we got clipped ," before stating that the two 737s had separated. Debris was then reported, with a pilot stating that a " whole winglet " had been torn off and was on the ground. Airport operations subsequently recovered the winglet , and both aircraft taxied back to their gates for inspection. An inbound Envoy Air aircraft was also ordered by ATC to go-around immediately after the incident.

In a statement to Simple Flying, American said that " the wingtips of both Boeing 737-800s made contact ," and that both planes had been taken out of service for maintenance inspections. The airline added that passengers on both flights would depart later on Friday evening. Tracking data shows that Flight 2152 left at around 11:00 PM, while Flight 638 departed at 11:20 PM, representing a delay of around six hours for both flights. An American spokesperson said
"While taxiing for departure at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), an American Airlines aircraft made contact with another American aircraft."

Hold short lines consist of four yellow lines painted across a taxiway before it meets a runway, and are there to prevent potentially dangerous runway incursions. Two solid lines are on the taxiway side, while two dashed lines are on the runway side. Pilots must stop before the solid lines unless ATC has cleared them to enter the runway.

The taxiway leading to DCA's Runway 19 is wide enough to accommodate two aircraft lined up side-by-side, an arrangement attempted by both jets on Friday. The 737-800 has a wingspan of 117 feet 5 inches (35.8 meters) including winglets, and pilots are expected to maintain situational awareness to ensure sufficient clearance from other aircraft.

The Federal Aviation Administration has confirmed it is investigating the incident, while the extent of the damage will determine whether the National Transportation Safety Board ( NTSB ) also becomes involved. Under the NTSB's definitions, an incident without serious injuries is only classified as an accident if an aircraft sustains " substantial damage ." Notably, this category specifically excludes damage to wingtips.
Multiple Ground Collisions At US Airports In Recent Weeks

Friday's incident is the latest in a series of ground collisions at major US airports in recent weeks. On November 14, a UPS Airlines Boeing 767 freighter and a Copa Airlines Boeing 737-800 collided at Miami International Airport (MIA) after the cargo jet taxied past the point where it had been instructed to give way.

On October 6, a Delta Air Lines Airbus A350 clipped the horizontal stabilizer of an Air Canada Boeing 777 being towed at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), leaving its winglet lodged in the 777's tail. Friday's collision also has similarities to an incident at DCA in April 2025, when two American Eagle regional jets clipped wings while waiting to depart, one of which had several members of Congress on board.
body_zh: 卢克拥有十多年的旅行作家和航空分析师经验。作为一名遍及中东和亚洲的热情旅行者，卢克对该行业提供了深刻的见解。总部位于东南亚。
周五晚上，美国航空的两架波音 737-800 飞机在罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场 (DCA) 的滑行道上排队时相撞，事故发生后的图像显示，其中一架飞机的小翼被撕裂。碰撞发生后不久，一名飞行员告诉空中交通管制中心（ATC），飞机“稍微越过了等待短线”，并与旁边的美国喷气式飞机“交换了油漆”。
事故发生在当地时间下午 5:10 左右，靠近 19 号跑道，涉及飞往达拉斯/沃斯堡国际机场 (DFW) 的美国航空 638 航班和飞往芝加哥奥黑尔国际机场 (ORD) 的美国航空 2152 航班。这是不到 20 个月内第二次两架美国品牌飞机在等待从 DCA 起飞时相撞，继 2025 年 4 月发生过类似的翼尖相撞事件。
美国 737 翼尖小翼在 DCA 碰撞中被撕裂
航班跟踪数据显示，两架 737 飞机均已滑出并排队等候进入 19 号跑道，而 2152 航班则排在 638 航班后面。当管制员指示 638 航班靠近跑道时，一名飞行员报告说，他们与另一架美国 737 飞机相撞，然后表示不确定这两架飞机是否仍连接在一起。
2152 航班上的一名飞行员随后证实，“哦，是的，我们被夹住了”，然后表示两架 737 飞机已经分离。随后报告了残骸，一名飞行员称“整个小翼”已被撕裂并掉落在地面上。机场运营部门随后收回了小翼，两架飞机都滑行回登机口接受检查。事件发生后，空中交通管制部门也命令一架入境特使航空飞机立即复飞。
美国航空在给 Simple Flying 的一份声明中表示，“两架波音 737-800 的翼尖发生了接触”，两架飞机均已停止运行以进行维护检查。该航空公司补充说，两趟航班的乘客将于周五晚上晚些时候出发。跟踪数据显示，2152 航班于晚上 11:00 左右起飞，638 航班于晚上 11:20 起飞，两趟航班均延误约 6 小时。美国发言人表示
“在罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场 (DCA) 滑行准备出发时，美国航空公司的一架飞机与另一架美国飞机发生了接触。”
等待短线由在滑行道与跑道相遇之前绘制的四条黄线组成，用于防止潜在危险的跑道侵入。两条实线位于滑行道一侧，两条虚线位于跑道一侧。飞行员必须在实线之前停下来，除非空中交通管制允许他们进入跑道。
通往 DCA 19 号跑道的滑行道足够宽，可以容纳两架并排的飞机，两架飞机周五都尝试过这种安排。 737-800 的翼展为 117 英尺 5 英寸（35.8 米），包括小翼，飞行员需要保持态势感知，以确保与其他飞机有足够的间隙。
美国联邦航空管理局已确认正在调查这起事件，而损害程度将决定国家运输安全委员会（NTSB）是否也参与其中。根据美国国家运输安全委员会的定义，没有严重伤害的事件只有在飞机遭受“重大损坏”时才被归类为事故。值得注意的是，此类别明确排除了翼尖损坏。
最近几周美国机场发生多起地面碰撞事故
周五的事件是最近几周美国主要机场发生的一系列地面碰撞事故中的最新一起。 11 月 14 日，UPS 航空公司的一架波音 767 货机与巴拿马航空公司的一架波音 737-800 货机在迈阿密国际机场 (MIA) 相撞，当时货机滑行经过了被指示让行的地点。
10 月 6 日，达美航空的一架空客 A350 飞机在洛杉矶国际机场 (LAX) 撞到了加拿大航空一架波音 777 飞机的水平安定面，导致其小翼卡在 777 机尾。周五的相撞事件也与 2025 年 4 月 DCA 发生的一起事件有相似之处，当时两架美国之鹰支线喷气式飞机在等待起飞时折断机翼，其中一架机上有几名国会议员。

title_en: The Airbus A350’s Unique Cabin Design That Sets It Apart From Others
title_zh: 空客 A350 独特的客舱设计使其与众不同
summary: The jet's cabin complements its exceptional long-range capabilities.
summary_zh: 该喷气式飞机的机舱与其卓越的远程能力相得益彰。
body_en: The leading independent voice for aviation news and insight.

The Airbus A350 has silently become one of the most recognizable long-haul aircraft in the skies today, but its most distinctive asset is likely not going to be its curved wingtips or ultra-efficient engines, but rather the aircraft's cabin itself. From the beginning, Airbus designed the A350's cross-section and interior architecture around overall passenger wellbeing, before wrapping that in the airline's 'Airspace' design language.

The aircraft features higher ceilings, wider sidewalls, and large overhead bins that all combine with low cabin noise, large windows, and advanced air management systems in order to create a noticeably calmer environment on long flights. Humidity and overall cabin pressure levels remain optimized to reduce jet lag and fatigue, while carefully engineered lighting schemes help allow passengers to adjust to new time zones.

Airlines, on the other hand, get a flexible interior shell that they can tune for all kinds of routes. As more carriers introduce refreshed Airbus A350 interiors and Airbus rolls out its New Production Standard with wider, longer cabins, the aircraft is increasingly beginning to set a benchmark for how a modern long-haul cabin should feel.

It also showcases why cabin design matters just as much as range or fuel burn for passengers and airlines alike. For many travellers, the first step onto an Airbus A350 instantly signals a different kind of widebody experience for passengers that an airline can market.

Originally launched as the Airbus XWB (which stands for 'eXtra-Wide-Body'), the A350 family was developed as a clean-sheet, long-range twin-engine aircraft designed to replace earlier four-engine types and to compete directly with the Boeing 787 and 777. Originally built from carbon-fibre reinforced plastic, the aircraft combines a lightweight fuselage with a high-aspect-ratio wing and Rolls-Royce Trent XWB engines.

These turbofans deliver double-digit fuel-burn and carbon emissions reductions over older widebodies. The family today spans the Airbus A350-900, the ultra-long-range Airbus A350-900ULR, and the stretched Airbus A350-1000, in addition to the forthcoming Airbus A350F freighter, giving airlines a common cockpit and systems across multiple mission profiles.

Typical three-class layouts seat roughly 300 to 380 passengers, with range figures comfortably exceeding 8,000 miles (12,875 km) on passenger variants. Airbus has continued to refine the platform using its New Production Standard, trimming weight across the board, and significantly improving take-off performance while unlocking extra usable cabin length and width.

The table above details some additional specifications for the Airbus A350 , according to documents published by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency. Orders have now passed 1,600, with hundreds already in service and a growing backlog from both established network carriers and fast-growing new market entrants.

Operational data now shows that the global Airbus A350 fleet has flown well over a million sectors on more than a thousand routes, with an excellent safety record and strong overall dispatch reliability. For airlines, that translates into the ability to open thinner long-haul city pairs while upgauging older fleets on trunk routes and standardizing on a single modern widebody family.

What differentiates the Airbus A350 most from its rivals is its Airspace cabin architecture. The fuselage cross-section was shaped to maximize usable interior width between the sidewalls, giving designers more shoulder room at seated eye level than earlier Airbus types and many competing jet models.

That extra space can thus be spent on wider seats, broader aisles, larger armrests, or a mix of all three, depending on each airline's philosophy. An improved cabin experience offers a lot of comfort and versatility for passengers, allowing airlines to charge more for these kinds of premium seats.

High ceilings, carefully sculpted sidewalls, and large pivoting overhead bins create a sense of openness while still giving generous space for passengers to easily stow carry-on bags. The cabin is also engineered for comfort on a microscopic level, with higher humidity, lower effective cabin altitude, and very low noise levels that all help reduce fatigue on long-haul overnight sectors.

With the latest New Production Standard, Airbus has subtly widened and stretched the cabin envelope. This has freed up space for larger galleys, new crew-rest arrangements, and ultimately additional seating options without the requirement to fundamentally change the feel of the aircraft's interior.

Combined with flexible lighting, advanced connectivity, and a step-by-step modification approach, the Airbus A350 offers airlines an unusually adaptable canvas for everything from minimalist economy layouts to highly differentiated four-class flagship aircraft.
What Makes The Airbus A350 Well-Suited For Premium Cabins?

The Airbus A350's geometry and flight control systems make it an unusually strong platform for offering premium cabin service. The aircraft's wide, oval-shaped cross-section supports spacious 1-2-1 business-class layouts that offer long beds and large side consoles that do not feel squeezed, all while leaving room for generous aisles and direct aisle access at every seat.

Lower overall cabin noise, advanced filtration, and higher humidity, all alongside a lower effective cabin altitude, all enhance sleep quality and overall well-being. This aligns nicely with what high-yield passengers are looking to get out of overnight flights. The New Production Standard adds roughly four inches of extra usable cabin width.

Airlines are already channeling this into wider privacy suites, door-equipped business seats, and more expansive premium-economy shells. Flag carriers are leaning heavily into this potential. Qantas is using a customized Airbus A350-1000ULR in order to house extra-spacious first and business cabins alongside a dedicated wellbeing zone on ultra-long-haul Project Sunrise flights.

SWISS is another airline that will use the aircraft to introduce new kinds of premium cabins, with the carrier debuting its new SWISS Senses four-class concept, which includes enclosed first-class suites and door-equipped business-class seats. These projects highlight how the Airbus A350 gives designers the room and range to build truly differentiated flagship products, turning the cabin into a competitive weapon on the world's longest and most lucrative routes.
body_zh: 航空新闻和见解的领先独立声音。
空客 A350 已悄然成为当今天空中最知名的长途飞机之一，但其最独特的资产可能不是其弯曲的翼尖或超高效的发动机，而是飞机的机舱本身。从一开始，空客就围绕乘客的整体健康状况设计了 A350 的横截面和内部结构，然后将其融入航空公司的“空域”设计语言中。
该飞机具有更高的天花板、更宽的侧壁和大型头顶行李箱，所有这些都与低机舱噪音、大窗户和先进的空气管理系统相结合，以便在长途飞行中创造一个明显更安静的环境。湿度和整体机舱压力水平保持优化，以减少时差和疲劳，而精心设计的照明方案有助于让乘客适应新的时区。
另一方面，航空公司拥有灵活的内部外壳，可以针对各种航线进行调整。随着越来越多的航空公司推出更新的空客 A350 内饰，以及空客推出客舱更宽、更长的新生产标准，该飞机越来越多地开始为现代长途客舱的感受设定基准。
它还展示了为什么客舱设计对于乘客和航空公司来说与航程或燃油消耗一样重要。对于许多旅客来说，踏上空客 A350 的第一步立即意味着航空公司可以为乘客提供一种不同的宽体客机体验。
A350 系列最初以空中客车 XWB（代表“超宽体”）的形式推出，是一款全新的远程双引擎飞机，旨在取代早期的四引擎机型，并与波音 787 和 777 直接竞争。该飞机最初采用碳纤维增强塑料制成，将轻质机身与高展弦比机翼和劳斯莱斯遄达 XWB 发动机结合在一起。
与老式宽体飞机相比，这些涡轮风扇发动机的燃油消耗和碳排放量减少了两位数。该系列目前涵盖空客 A350-900、超远程空客 A350-900ULR 和加长型空客 A350-1000，以及即将推出的空客 A350F 货机，为航空公司提供跨多个任务配置的通用驾驶舱和系统。
典型的三舱布局可容纳大约 300 至 380 名乘客，乘客型号的航程数字轻松超过 8,000 英里（12,875 公里）。空中客车公司继续利用其新生产标准完善该平台，全面减轻重量，显着提高起飞性能，同时释放额外的可用客舱长度和宽度。
根据欧盟航空安全局发布的文件，上表详细介绍了空客 A350 的一些附加规格。目前订单已超过 1,600 份，其中数百份已投入使用，老牌网络运营商和快速增长的新市场进入者的积压订单不断增加。
目前运营数据显示，空客A350全球机队已飞越超过100万个航段、1000多条航线，具有出色的安全记录和强大的整体调度可靠性。对于航空公司来说，这意味着能够开通更精简的长途城市航线，同时升级干线航线上的旧机队，并对单一的现代宽体机系列进行标准化。
空客 A350 与其竞争对手的最大区别在于其空域客舱架构。机身横截面的形状最大限度地提高了侧壁之间的可用内部宽度，为设计师提供了比早期空客机型和许多竞争喷气式飞机更多的肩部空间。
因此，额外的空间可以用于更宽的座位、更宽的过道、更大的扶手，或三者的组合，具体取决于每家航空公司的理念。改善的客舱体验为乘客提供了更多的舒适度和多功能性，从而使航空公司可以对此类高级座椅收取更高的费用。
高高的天花板、精心雕刻的侧壁和大型旋转头顶行李箱营造出开放感，同时仍为乘客提供宽敞的空间，方便存放随身行李。客舱的设计还考虑到了微观层面的舒适性，具有更高的湿度、更低的有效客舱高度以及极低的噪音水平，这些都有助于减轻长途过夜航段的疲劳。
根据最新的新生产标准，空客巧妙地加宽和拉伸了机舱围护结构。这为更大的厨房、新的机组人员休息安排以及最终的额外座位选择腾出了空间，而无需从根本上改变飞机内部的感觉。
结合灵活的照明、先进的连接性和逐步的改装方法，空客 A350 为航空公司提供了一个异常适应性强的画布，适用于从简约的经济布局到高度差异化的四级旗舰飞机的各种用途。
空客 A350 为何非常适合高级客舱？
空客 A350 的几何形状和飞行控制系统使其成为提供优质客舱服务的异常强大的平台。该飞机宽阔的椭圆形横截面支持宽敞的 1-2-1 商务舱布局，提供长床和不会感到挤压的大型侧控制台，同时为宽敞的过道和每个座位的直接过道通道留出空间。
较低的整体客舱噪音、先进的过滤和较高的湿度，以及较低的有效客舱高度，都可以提高睡眠质量和整体福祉。这与高收益乘客希望从夜间航班中得到的东西非常吻合。新生产标准增加了大约四英寸的额外可用客舱宽度。
航空公司已经将其应用到更宽敞的隐私套房、配有门的商务座椅和更宽敞的高级经济舱。旗舰航空公司正在大力挖掘这一潜力。澳洲航空正在使用定制的空客 A350-1000ULR 来容纳超宽敞的头等舱和商务舱，以及超长途“日出计划”航班上的专用健康区。
瑞航是另一家将利用这架飞机推出新型高级客舱的航空公司，该公司首次推出了全新的 SWISS Senses 四舱概念，其中包括封闭式头等舱套房和配有门的商务舱座椅。这些项目凸显了空客 A350 如何为设计师提供空间和范围来打造真正差异化的旗舰产品，将客舱变成世界上最长和最有利可图的航线上的竞争武器。

title_en: 5 Mid-Sized US Airport Projects Quietly Adding Gates & Merging Security Checkpoints In 2026
title_zh: 美国 5 个中型机场项目将于 2026 年悄然增加登机口并合并安全检查站
summary: From Omaha’s new gates to Spokane’s $335 million Central Hall, five mid-sized US airports are adding gates and merging security checkpoints.
summary_zh: 从奥马哈的新登机口到斯波坎耗资 3.35 亿美元的中央大厅，美国五个中型机场正在增加登机口并合并安全检查站。
body_en: Brandon's passion for aviation started at a young age. He became involved in the flight simulator and VATSIM communities, which sparked his interest in aviation and eventually led him to earn his private pilot license. Outside of work, he continues to build flight hours, explore new airports, and stay involved in the aviation community.

Billion-dollar terminal programs at Chicago , Los Angeles, and New York tend to dominate airport construction headlines, but some of the most practical upgrades in the country are happening one tier down. Medium-sized airports that grew quickly over the last decade are now dealing with the same problem: too few gates for the flights airlines want to add, and terminals split into separate wings that each need their own security checkpoint. For passengers, that layout often means picking the right checkpoint before knowing which gate is free, and for airlines, it limits where new service can go.

The five projects below take different routes to the same goal. Some add gates, others knock down the walls between concourses so a single checkpoint can feed every gate, and a few do both. Each has also hit a visible milestone in 2026, whether that is new gates opening to passengers, a finished concourse, a design contract, or steel rising on a replacement terminal, even though most of the work will not wrap up until 2028 or 2029.

Eppley Airfield (OMA) in Omaha is the furthest along of the projects on this list. In November 2026, passengers got their first look at the $950 million Build OMA Terminal Modernization Program, which the Omaha Airport Authority approved to nearly double the terminal's size. According to Travel Weekly , the building will grow from 375,000 square feet (34,839 square meters) to 646,000 square feet (60,015 square meters), and the expansion adds two gates for international flights along with a customs hall. Holder Construction is managing the work, which broke ground in February 2024 on a terminal that had not been modernized since the 1980s.

Four new gates, numbered A1, A1A, A1B and A2, opened on November 4, 2026. Airways Magazine reported that Delta Air Lines was using the new space in place of its previous south concourse gates, with passengers reaching the area through the existing south terminal and its current checkpoint, an arrangement that will only last until the rest of the building opens. Once finished, the unified concourse will connect the terminal areas that are separated today, and every departing passenger will clear a centralized TSA checkpoint in a new central pavilion that also houses a food court and shops.

The timeline beyond that is already set. Airways reports that the central pavilion and more of the concourse should open in early 2027, followed by new baggage and ticketing systems in mid-2027, and WOWT reported that the full program remains on time and on budget for completion in 2028. Steady demand is driving the work. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) data shows Eppley enplaned 2,565,135 passengers in 2025, a 0.70% dip from the prior year, but the airport still set a monthly record of 530,157 passengers in June 2026, according to WOWT. Construction stood at 60% complete in September 2026.
From concourse C to a $335 million central hall

Spokane International Airport (GEG) technically sits in the FAA’s small hub category, with 2,106,307 enplanements in 2025, but it is the second-busiest airport in Washington and runs a terminal program on a medium-hub scale. Its Terminal Renovation and Expansion program, known as TREX, began with a $150 million expansion of Concourse C. The first part, Concourse C West, opened in May 2024 with three new gates and six new ticket counters. The second part, Concourse C East, replaced ground boarding with three new passenger boarding bridges at gates C1 through C3, and the airport announced the full Concourse C project complete on May 26, 2026.

That finished concourse sets up the larger second phase. Today, Spokane operates two siloed terminals, so passengers screen separately for the A and B concourses or for Concourse C. The new Central Hall will consolidate security screening for all airlines into one checkpoint and add a post-security hall connecting all three concourses. As the Spokesman-Review reports, the building will place baggage claim on the ground floor and security screening on the second. Utility relocation along the front curb began in May 2026 to clear the site.

The scope has grown considerably since planning began, both in floor area and in cost. A January 2023 filing with Washington’s Department of Enterprise Services described a 145,000-square-foot (13,471 square meters) Central Hall with an estimated maximum price of $152 million. The Journal of Business now puts the project at 255,000 square feet (23,690 square meters) and an estimated $335 million. Simple Flying has detailed how the hall will end repeat screening by 2030. Growth explains the larger footprint, since by then the airport expects roughly 6.2 million annual passengers, according to the Daily Journal of Commerce .
Credit: John Glenn Columbus International Airport

The largest project here belongs to John Glenn Columbus International Airport (CMH). The CMH Next program is a roughly $2 billion replacement terminal, and WHIO noted it is the most expensive public works project ever undertaken in Franklin County. Columbus also leads this group in traffic by a wide margin, with 4,396,625 enplanements in 2025 according to the FAA, and the Columbus Regional Airport Authority reported nearly 9.4 million passengers across its airports that year. The existing terminal opened in 1958 and will be demolished once the new building is ready.

Unlike Omaha and Spokane, Columbus is not stitching older buildings together. Spectrum News reported that the approved plan includes a 36-gate terminal and a central marketplace with just one security checkpoint, replacing the three checkpoints the airport operates today. According to Construction Equipment Guide , those 36 gates are seven more than CMH currently uses, and two will handle international flights with on-site customs facilities . Gensler designed the building, which comes in at just over 1 million square feet (92,903 square meters) and adds 40% to 60% more waiting area at the gates, according to Archinect .

Progress in 2026 is mostly structural, with crews now working vertically on the terminal itself. Construction began in December 2024, focused first on a new elevated roadway, and the first steel beam for the building went up on August 8, 2025. Construction Equipment Guide reported in October 2026 that the authority now expects completion in January 2029. That date is deliberate, since Axios notes that the opening is timed to coincide with the airport’s 100th anniversary. Once the move happens, the old terminal site will become additional overnight parking for aircraft, letting airlines position more planes for early morning departures.
body_zh: 布兰登从小就对航空充满热情。他参与了飞行模拟器和 VATSIM 社区，这激发了他对航空的兴趣，并最终使他获得了私人飞行员执照。工作之余，他继续增加飞行时间、探索新机场并继续参与航空界。
芝加哥、洛杉矶和纽约耗资数十亿美元的航站楼项目往往占据机场建设的头条新闻，但该国一些最实用的升级项目正在下一层进行。过去十年快速发展的中型机场现在也面临着同样的问题：登机口太少，无法满足航空公司想要增加的航班的需求，而且航站楼分成不同的翼楼，每个翼楼都需要自己的安全检查站。对于乘客来说，这种布局通常意味着在知道哪个登机口是空闲的之前选择正确的检查站，而对于航空公司来说，它限制了新服务的去向。
以下五个项目采取不同的路线来实现同一目标。有些增加了大门，另一些则拆除了大厅之间的墙壁，这样一个检查站就可以满足每个大门的需求，还有一些则两者兼而有之。每个项目都在 2026 年达到了一个明显的里程碑，无论是向乘客开放的新登机口、完工的大厅、设计合同，还是更换航站楼的钢架，尽管大部分工作要到 2028 年或 2029 年才能完成。

奥马哈的埃普利机场 (OMA) 是此列表中距离最远的项目。 2026 年 11 月，乘客们首次看到耗资 9.5 亿美元建设 OMA 航站楼现代化计划，奥马哈机场管理局批准该计划将航站楼规模扩大近一倍。据《旅游周刊》报道，该建筑面积将从 375,000 平方英尺（34,83​​9 平方米）增至 646,000 平方英尺（60,015 平方米），扩建后增加了两个国际航班登机口和一个海关大厅。该工程由 Holder Construction 负责管理，该工程于 2024 年 2 月在一座自 20 世纪 80 年代以来从未进行过现代化改造的航站楼破土动工。
编号为 A1、A1A、A1B 和 A2 的四个新登机口于 2026 年 11 月 4 日启用。《航空杂志》报道称，达美航空正在使用新空间代替之前的南大厅登机口，乘客通过现有南航站楼及其当前检查站到达该区域，这种安排只会持续到大楼其余部分开放为止。建成后，统一大厅将连接目前分开的航站楼区域，每位离境旅客将通过新中央展馆内的 TSA 集中检查站，该展馆还设有美食广场和商店。

超出此范围的时间表已经确定。航空公司报告称，中央展馆和大厅的更多部分将于 2027 年初开放，新的行李和票务系统将于 2027 年中期开放，WOWT 报告称，整个项目仍按时、按预算完成，将于 2028 年完成。稳定的需求正在推动这项工作。 WOWT 的数据显示，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 的数据显示，埃普利机场 2025 年载客量为 2,565,135 名乘客，比上年下降 0.70%，但该机场在 2026 年 6 月仍创下了 530,157 名乘客的月度记录。 2026 年 9 月，施工进度已完成 60%。
从 C 大厅到耗资 3.35 亿美元的中央大厅

从技术上讲，斯波坎国际机场 (GEG) 属于 FAA 的小型枢纽类别，到 2025 年将有 2,106,307 架飞机，但它是华盛顿第二繁忙的机场，并运行中型枢纽规模的航站楼项目。其航站楼改造和扩建计划（称为 TREX）从耗资 1.5 亿美元扩建 C 大厅开始。第一部分 C 西大厅于 2024 年 5 月开业，设有三个新登机口和六个新售票柜台。第二部分，C 东大厅，在 C1 至 C3 登机口用三座新的旅客登机桥取代了地面登机，机场宣布整个 C 大厅项目将于 2026 年 5 月 26 日竣工。
完工的大厅建立了更大的第二阶段。如今，斯波坎运营着两个孤立的航站楼，因此乘客可以分别对 A 和 B 大厅或 C 大厅进行安检。新的中央大厅将把所有航空公司的安检整合到一个检查站，并增加一个连接所有三个大厅的安检后大厅。据《发言人评论》报道，该大楼将在一楼设置行李提取处，在二楼设置安检处。 2026 年 5 月开始沿前路缘进行公用设施搬迁，以清理场地。

自规划开始以来，无论是建筑面积还是成本，范围都大幅扩大。 2023 年 1 月向华盛顿企业服务部提交的一份文件描述了一座占地 145,000 平方英尺（13,471 平方米）的中央大厅，估计最高价格为 1.52 亿美元。据《商业杂志》报道，该项目面积为 255,000 平方英尺（23,690 平方米），估计价值 3.35 亿美元。 Simple Flying 详细介绍了到 2030 年该大厅将如何结束重复安检。 据《商业日报》报道，增长解释了占地面积更大的原因，因为到那时机场预计每年约有 620 万名乘客。
图片来源：约翰·格伦哥伦布国际机场

这里最大的项目属于约翰格伦哥伦布国际机场（CMH）。 CMH Next 计划是一个价值约 20 亿美元的替换航站楼，WHIO 指出，这是富兰克林县有史以来最昂贵的公共工程项目。根据美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 的数据，哥伦布在客流量方面也遥遥领先，到 2025 年将有 4,396,625 架飞机起飞，哥伦布地区机场管理局报告称，当年其机场的乘客量接近 940 万人次。现有航站楼于 1958 年启用，新大楼竣工后将被拆除。

与奥马哈和斯波坎不同，哥伦布并没有将旧建筑缝合在一起。 Spectrum News 报道称，批准的计划包括一个有 36 个登机口的航站楼和一个只有一个安全检查站的中央市场，取代了机场目前运营的三个检查站。据《建筑设备指南》称，这 36 个登机口比 CMH 目前使用的登机口多了 7 个，其中 2 个将通过现场海关设施处理国际航班。据 Archinect 称，Gensler 设计的这座建筑面积刚刚超过 100 万平方英尺（92,903 平方米），并增加了 40% 至 60% 的门口等候区。

2026 年的进展主要是结构性的，工作人员现在在航站楼本身垂直工作。施工于 2024 年 12 月开始，首先关注的是一条新的高架道路，该建筑的第一根钢梁于 2025 年 8 月 8 日架起。《建筑设备指南》在 2026 年 10 月报道称，当局目前预计于 2029 年 1 月竣工。这个日期是经过深思熟虑的，因为 Axios 指出，开业时间恰逢机场成立 100 周年。一旦搬迁完成，旧航站楼将成为额外的飞机夜间停放处，让航空公司可以停放更多飞机以供清晨起飞。

title_en: Boeing to win lion’s share of Qantas widebody order over Airbus: Bloomberg
title_zh: 彭博社：波音将超越空客赢得澳洲航空宽体机订单的最大份额
summary: Boeing is set to win the lion’s share of a potential Qantas widebody order over European rival Airbus,… The post Boeing to win lion’s share of Qantas widebody order over Airbus: Bloomberg appeared first on AeroTime .
summary_zh: 波音公司将击败欧洲竞争对手空客公司，赢得澳洲航空潜在宽体机订单的最大份额，……波音将赢得澳洲航空的最大份额
body_en: Boeing is set to win the lion’s share of a potential Qantas widebody order over European rival Airbus, according to Bloomberg.
On November 27, 2026, Bloomberg claimed that an order for 20 aircraft from the Australian flag carrier is set to include Boeing 787 Dreamliners and some Airbus A350s.
The information is said to have been sourced from people with knowledge of developments involving the order.
In a statement to Bloomberg, Qantas said: “We are still in discussion with the relevant aircraft manufacturers as part of our widebody fleet planning and no decisions have been made.”
This is not the first time that speculation of a potential new Qantas widebody order has circulated this year.
In June 2026, Reuters spoke with industry sources who said Qantas was looking at an order for 20 aircraft with both the 787 and A350 under consideration.
Qantas A380 retirement and upcoming A350-1000ULRs

Qantas announced in August 2026 that its fleet of Airbus A380s would retire four years earlier than originally planned. They were expected to fly until at least until 2032, but this has now been brought forward to 2028.
With the A380 retirement in mind, Qantas will want to ensure it has additional long-haul aircraft capacity for the years ahead.
In April 2027, the first of 12 Airbus A350-1000ULR aircraft is due to join the airline, once all final tests have been completed.
The aircraft has just 238 seats – according to Qantas, the “lowest seat density of any A350 around the world” – and is designed to give travelers more space.
The A350-1000ULRs will focus on ultra-long-haul routes such as Sydney Airport (SYD) to London-Heathrow Airport (LHR).
The post Boeing to win lion’s share of Qantas widebody order over Airbus: Bloomberg appeared first on AeroTime .
body_zh: 据彭博社报道，波音公司将击败欧洲竞争对手空客公司，赢得澳洲航空潜在宽体客机订单的最大份额。
2026 年 11 月 27 日，彭博社声称，这家澳大利亚旗舰航空公司订购了 20 架飞机，其中包括波音 787 梦想飞机和一些空客 A350。
据称，这些信息来自了解该订单事态发展的人士。
澳洲航空在给彭博社的一份声明中表示：“作为我们宽体机队规划的一部分，我们仍在与相关飞机制造商进行讨论，但尚未做出任何决定。”
这并不是今年第一次有关于澳洲航空可能获得新宽体机订单的猜测。
2026 年 6 月，路透社采访业内消息人士称，澳洲航空正在考虑订购 20 架飞机，其中包括 787 和 A350。
澳洲航空 A380 退役和即将推出的 A350-1000ULR
澳洲航空于 2026 年 8 月宣布，其空客 A380 机队将比原计划提前四年退役。预计它们至少会飞行到 2032 年，但现在已提前到 2028 年。
考虑到 A380 的退役，澳洲航空希望确保未来几年拥有额外的长途飞机运力。
2027 年 4 月，所有最终测试完成后，12 架空客 A350-1000ULR 飞机中的第一架将加入该航空公司。
该飞机仅有 238 个座位——据澳洲航空称，这是“全球 A350 中座位密度最低的”——旨在为旅客提供更多空间。
A350-1000ULR 将专注于超长途航线，例如悉尼机场 (SYD) 至伦敦希思罗机场 (LHR)。
波音公司击败空客公司赢得了澳洲航空宽体飞机订单的最大份额：彭博社首先出现在 AeroTime 上。

title_en: The New Airbus A220 Coming In 2027
title_zh: 全新空客 A220 将于 2027 年推出
summary: A high-density model is set to enter service next year.
summary_zh: 高密度模型将于明年投入使用。
body_en: The leading independent voice for aviation news and insight.

The Airbus A220 is currently preparing for a major upgrade, although the manufacturer is falling short of launching a new variant altogether. This year, new Airbus A220 deliveries will be outfitted with the manufacturer's Airspace interior, aligning the A220 with the interior feel of the A350, A330neo, and A320neo. Highlights include new upgraded extra-large overhead lockers, which will be around 20% lighter while offering more than 15% additional baggage capacity.

These aircraft will also feature 16-million-color LED lighting, allowing airlines to tailor their brand or flight phases. Airbus also plans on offering this unique interior as a retrofit option for existing Airbus A220 customers. Meanwhile, starting in 2027, a higher-density Airbus A220-300, one that features a 160-seat layout, will be offered, which provides operators with additional revenue and unit-cost gains without introducing a larger model to any given route.

However, the much-discussed Airbus A220-500 variant remains unannounced, and it does not look like Airbus has any plans to make any quick moves there as well. The manufacturer has looked to continue improving the profitability of the Airbus A220 family while also improving production rates, offering even more flexibility for operators. Let's analyze all the upcoming changes to the Airbus A220 family.

To contextualize the upcoming upgrades to this extremely popular aircraft program, it is important to begin by breaking down the Airbus A220's origins and discussing the aircraft's industrial footprint. The Airbus A220 began its life as a member of the Bombardier CSeries, a five-abreast narrowbody jet which was launched on July 13, 2008, with the intent of bridging the gap between regional jets and larger single-aisle aircraft.

It was first introduced to the market as the CS100, and it first took to the skies on September 16, 2013, before being certified by Transport Canada on December 18, 2015. The jet entered service with SWISS on July 15, 2016. The Bombardier CS300, which flew on February 27, 2015, would be certified on July 11, 2016, and it entered service on December 14 of that year with launch customer airBaltic.\

In July 2018, after Airbus took a majority stake in the company, it was quickly rebranded as the Airbus A220 and later organized as Airbus Canada Limited Partnership in June 2019. The aircraft program was now fully in the hands of manufacturing giant Airbus. The manufacturer's industrial capacity was expanded beyond Mirabel, Quebec, with a second final assembly line opened in Mobile, Alabama, in August 2019.

This allowed the manufacturer to avoid hefty import duties from US regulators. The manufacturer's ownership stake was increased to 75% in February 2020, with Bombardier electing to exit the program. The Airbus A220 remains the only commercial program managed by the manufacturer entirely outside of Europe. After entering service, the aircraft quickly established itself as offering strong dispatch reliability and improved passenger satisfaction over other models.

The Airbus A220 is powered by Pratt & Whitney PW1500G geared turbofan engines, and the aircraft offers a carbon-composite lightweight wing and an aluminum-lithium fuselage. Fly-by-wire controls and refined aerodynamics help deliver long legs and low-cost operations. Family weights range from 63 to 71 tonnes (139,000-156,000 lbs) of maximum takeoff weight (MTOW).

The aircraft family offers a range of 6,390-6,670 km (3,450-3,600 nautical miles), making it capable of serving almost all transcontinental niches in the United States and even longer-range lower-gauge routes within Europe. The 35 m (115 ft) Airbus A220-100 seats around 108-133 passengers, while the longer A220-300 seats a larger 130-160 passengers, depending on the specific configuration.

Airbus also launched the ACJ TwoTwenty business-jet variant, which was launched in late 2020. Delta remains the largest customer for the aircraft, and, globally, more than 1,100 Airbus A220s have been ordered, with over 500 delivered to date.

Globally, the fleet has surpassed 1.5 million flights and 2.7 million block hours, with the aircraft carrying more than 100 million passengers. The aircraft has also managed to maintain an exceptional safety reputation, with only one non-fatal smoke-related accident showing up on its rap sheet. It mainly competes with the Embraer E-Jet E2 family, holding a 55% share in this small-airliner niche, demonstrating the success and competitive value this program offers.

The A220 has slowly matured from being a promising upstart in the industry to becoming a core single-aisle workhorse for most carriers, especially with airlines wanting more revenue, lower unit costs, and a cabin that matches the rest of the manufacturer's portfolio. The five-abreast Airbus A220 already offers exceptional passenger comfort and impressive fuel burn, but bin space, lighting, and brand cohesion lag behind the newest Airbus models . Bringing the Airspace cabin to the aircraft helps close this gap.

Airlines today are extremely focused on premium and brand perception, and improving interiors is a key element of this overall strategy. From a commercial perspective, airlines need a low-risk way to add seats without adding a new aircraft type. The 160-seat Airbus A220-300 adds about ten more seats while providing more attractive costs per available seat mile, which ultimately proved useful for capacity-constrained layouts where upgauging to an A320neo would negatively impact profitability.

From a strategic perspective, Airbus needs to widen the A220's overall addressable market and strengthen the plane's business case before choosing to green-light a stretch to the Airbus A220-500. After all, the manufacturer wants to continue improving cabin appeal for legacy operators first.

Throughout this retrofitting and upgrade process, Airbus is mainly looking to pull two key levers. This year, new Airbus A220 deliveries will adopt the new Airbus Airspace cabin, a similar design that has been seen on Airbus A350, Airbus A330neo, and Airbus A320neo jets. Headlines are quick to discuss the 16-million-color LED lighting, which brand-matches the ambiance and circadian cues across different flight phases.

However, the Airspace kit also standardizes modern trim, surfaces, and touchpoints so that the aircraft will resemble any other Airbus model as closely as possible. Airbus is also quick to point out that it will be offering flexibility to operators, specifically when it comes to high-density Airbus A220-300 models. This ensures that its upgrades are not only providing optionality to future customers, but also letting existing operators improve their fleets.
body_zh: 航空新闻和见解的领先独立声音。
空客 A220 目前正在准备进行重大升级，尽管制造商尚未完全推出新型号。今年，新交付的空客 A220 将配备制造商的 Airspace 内饰，使 A220 与 A350、A330neo 和 A320neo 的内饰风格保持一致。亮点包括全新升级的超大头顶储物柜，重量减轻约 20%，同时行李容量增加超过 15%。
这些飞机还将配备 1600 万色 LED 照明，使航空公司能够定制其品牌或飞行阶段。空中客车公司还计划为现有的空中客车 A220 客户提供这种独特的内饰作为改装选项。与此同时，从 2027 年开始，将提供更高密度的空中客车 A220-300（具有 160 个座位的布局），这将为运营商提供额外的收入和单位成本收益，而无需在任何特定航线上引入更大的型号。
然而，备受讨论的空客 A220-500 改型仍未公布，而且空客似乎也没有任何计划在该领域采取任何快速行动。该制造商希望继续提高空客 A220 系列的盈利能力，同时提高生产率，为运营商提供更大的灵活性。让我们分析一下空客 A220 系列即将发生的所有变化。
为了了解这一极其受欢迎的飞机项目即将进行的升级，首先要分解空客 A220 的起源并讨论该飞机的工业足迹，这一点很重要。空客 A220 最初是庞巴迪 C 系列的一员，这是一款五并排窄体喷气机，于 2008 年 7 月 13 日推出，旨在缩小支线喷气机与大型单通道飞机之间的差距。
它首次以 CS100 的名称推向市场，于 2013 年 9 月 16 日首飞，并于 2015 年 12 月 18 日获得加拿大交通部认证。该飞机于 2016 年 7 月 15 日开始在瑞航服役。庞巴迪 CS300 于 2015 年 2 月 27 日首飞，将于 2016 年 7 月 11 日获得认证，并于 12 月投入运营。同年 14 月与启动客户波罗的海航空合作。\
2018年7月，空中客车公司取得该公司多数股权后，迅速更名为空中客车A220，并于2019年6月组建为空中客车加拿大有限合伙企业。该飞机项目现已完全掌握在制造巨头空中客车公司手中。该制造商的工业产能已扩展到魁北克米拉贝尔以外的地区，并于 2019 年 8 月在阿拉巴马州莫比尔市开设了第二条总装线。
这使得制造商能够避免美国监管机构征收的高额进口关税。 2020 年 2 月，该制造商的所有权股份增加至 75%，庞巴迪选择退出该计划。空客 A220 仍然是唯一一个完全由欧洲以外的制造商管理的商业项目。投入运营后，与其他机型相比，该飞机很快就确立了其强大的调度可靠性和更高的乘客满意度的地位。
空客 A220 由普惠 PW1500G 齿轮涡轮风扇发动机提供动力，该飞机配备碳复合材料轻型机翼和铝锂机身。电传操纵系统和精致的空气动力学设计有助于实现长航程和低成本运营。系列重量范围为最大起飞重量 (MTOW) 63 至 71 吨（139,000-156,000 磅）。
该飞机系列的航程为 6,390-6,670 公里（3,450-3,600 海里），使其能够服务于美国几乎所有的跨大陆航线，甚至欧洲境内的远程低轨航线。 35 m（115 英尺）长的空客 A220-100 可容纳约 108-133 名乘客，而较长的 A220-300 可容纳 130-160 名乘客，具体取决于具体配置。
空客还推出了 ACJ TwoTwenty 公务机改型，该型号于 2020 年底推出。达美航空仍然是该飞机的最大客户，全球已订购 1,100 多架空客 A220，迄今为止已交付 500 多架。
在全球范围内，该机队的航班数量已超过 150 万次，飞行时间超过 270 万小时，载客量超过 1 亿人次。该飞机还成功地保持了卓越的安全声誉，仅发生过一起与烟雾相关的非致命事故。它主要与巴西航空工业公司 E-Jet E2 系列竞争，在这一小型客机市场中占有 55% 的份额，展示了该计划所提供的成功和竞争价值。
A220 已经慢慢成熟，从业界有前途的新贵发展成为大多数航空公司的核心单通道主力飞机，特别是对于希望获得更多收入、降低单位成本以及与制造商其他产品组合相匹配的客舱的航空公司。五并排的空客 A220 已经为乘客提供了卓越的舒适度和令人印象深刻的燃油消耗，但行李箱空间、照明和品牌凝聚力落后于最新的空客机型。将空域舱引入飞机有助于缩小这一差距。
当今的航空公司非常注重高端和品牌认知，而改善内饰是这一整体战略的关键要素。从商业角度来看，航空公司需要一种低风险的方式来增加座位而不增加新的机型。 160 座的空客 A220-300 增加了大约 10 个座位，同时每可用座位英里的成本更具吸引力，最终证明这对于容量有限的布局很有用，因为升级到 A320neo 会对盈利能力产生负面影响。
从战略角度来看，空中客车公司需要扩大 A220 的整体潜在市场并加强飞机的商业案例，然后才选择向空中客车 A220-500 延伸。毕竟，制造商首先希望继续提高客舱对传统运营商的吸引力。
在整个改造和升级过程中，空客主要希望拉动两个关键杠杆。今年，新交付的空客 A220 将采用新的空客空域客舱，该设计与空客 A350、空客 A330neo 和空客 A320neo 喷气式飞机上的设计类似。头条新闻很快就讨论了 1600 万色 LED 照明，它与不同飞行阶段的氛围和昼夜节律线索相匹配。
然而，空域套件还标准化了现代装饰、表面和接触点，以便飞机尽可能类似于任何其他空客型号。空客还很快指出，它将为运营商提供灵活性，特别是在高密度空客 A220-300 机型方面。这确保了其升级不仅为未来客户提供了选择，而且还让现有运营商改进了他们的机队。

title_en: The Airbus A380 Burns Over 3,000 Gallons An Hour & Still Pays Off For Emirates
title_zh: 空客 A380 每小时燃烧超过 3,000 加仑，仍然为阿联酋航空带来回报
summary: Even with a staggering fuel burn, the A380 still lives on at Emirates.
summary_zh: 尽管燃油消耗惊人，A380 仍然在阿联酋航空服役。
body_en: Airline and Airport Management Graduate, Student Commercial Pilot and Commercial Aviation Writer.

The Airbus A380 burns far more than 3,000 gallons (approximately 11,356 liters) of fuel every single hour, significantly higher than what would be expected from a modern widebody aircraft. Despite the high figure, Emirates keeps the four-engine superjumbo central to its long-haul network. Across the wider airline industry, most carriers have scaled back, parked, or retired their double-deckers because four engines bring steep fuel burn and heavy maintenance demands on ordinary routes. Emirates has defied this trend and continues to fly the aircraft across major global trunk routes, honing the high hourly consumption into a core element of its commercial strategy.

How can an airframe that consumes thousands of gallons per hour still pay off when other airlines view it as a commercial liability? Success ultimately comes from filling hundreds of seats on flights into slot-constrained airports backed by strong connecting hub traffic. Looking closely at the A380's fuel burn, per-seat economics, hub advantages, financial track record, and future outlook, it becomes clear that the type still makes sense for Emirates.

On an hourly basis, the A380's fuel consumption stands out immediately against modern twin-engine long-haul aircraft. Figures cited by Simple Flying place the A380's fuel burn at roughly 4,600 gallons (approximately 17,413 liters) per hour, nearly double the roughly 2,700 gallons (approximately 10,221 liters) per hour burned by an Airbus A350-1000. That wide gap stems from four large turbofans moving a heavier double-deck airframe across long sectors, where takeoff weight, cruise altitude, headwinds, and route length continually shape exact hourly consumption.

Emirates President Tim Clark has framed that hourly fuel burn in weight terms as well as volume, as noted by Airline Ratings. On a long-haul flight from Dubai International Airport (DXB) to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) carrying 515 passengers, Clark has indicated that fuel burn runs around 13 tonnes (approximately 28,660 pounds) per hour. Across the full trip between the two hubs, total fuel burn reaches roughly 200 tonnes (approximately 440,925 pounds).

Those figures show why the A380 looks daunting whenever an airline evaluates raw fuel burn in isolation rather than total seat capacity. Burning that much fuel every hour creates a substantial fuel bill on paper, which will naturally lead most airlines to look elsewhere for widebody capacity. With that in mind, it seems somewhat nonsensical for Emirates to stick with the A380 when all its rivals have ceded to the extortionate costs.

Once fuel burn is divided across hundreds of seats, not just being viewed purely per hour, the A380's commercial math changes sharply. Using the Dubai-to-Los Angeles comparison noted by AirlineRatings, Emirates President Tim Clark has explained that the A380's fuel cost per seat can beat running two Boeing 787 flights, each of which burns roughly half as much fuel as the superjumbo. That advantage holds when high load factors keep cabins well filled, whereas flying a large double-decker with dozens of empty seats quickly destroys per-passenger efficiency.

Slot-constrained airports turn that high seat count into an even bigger practical asset on trunk routes. As The Economist reports , scarce runway and terminal slots at congested hubs such as London Heathrow (LHR) and Hong Kong (HKG) limit how often an airline can land or take off. Putting a 787 into a single Heathrow slot where a 517-seat A380 can operate leaves far fewer seats for sale at peak demand, not something that Emirates sees as acceptable.

Emirates reinforces those slot economics through its connecting hub in Dubai , which pulls transfer passengers from across continents onto high-capacity long-haul flights. Whereas other major airports focus on point-to-point local demand at either end of a route, Dubai funnels connecting traffic into large cabins, so seat occupancy stays consistently high. Together, scarce slots at major destinations and steady transfer flows at Dubai give Emirates the passenger volume needed to make high seat counts pay off.

Few other carriers share the exact combination of network scale, slot pressure, and hub geography that lets Emirates run the A380 so consistently. Reporting from Simple Flying highlights that Emirates built its entire long-haul model around funneling global connecting traffic through Dubai onto high-capacity trunk routes. Many other airlines rely more heavily on local point-to-point demand or spread flying across fragmented secondary markets, where filling 500 seats every day is much harder to do consistently.

Differences in hub structure and slot portfolios also explain why rival operators often reach different conclusions about the double-decker. While some airlines face tight runway caps at destinations, they may lack a central connecting hub with the same global reach or fleet concentration to keep large cabins full across seasons. When demand dips or seasonal swings hit, carrying hundreds of empty seats penalizes operating margins far more severely than operating smaller twin-aisle jets.

Those structural contrasts help explain why several carriers have parked or retired A380 aircraft earlier than Emirates, and why others have not made the A380 the focal point of their fleet. Take Air France, for example : the airline retired all its A380 aircraft in 2020 , primarily because it could not fill seats like Emirates can. Without Emirates' specific mix of connecting scale and high-volume trunk demand, replicating its A380 formula remains out of reach for most airlines.

The A380's commercial case at Emirates is backed by years of financial results, not just theoretical seat math. Before the pandemic, Emirates President Tim Clark told Simple Flying that roughly 85% of Emirates' profits came from the A380 because the double-decker stayed consistently full and drew strong demand across every cabin. High occupancy across first, business, and economy turned those large passenger counts into substantial earnings across long-haul trunk routes.

That profit contribution has carried into Emirates' modern record run even as fuel expenses and operating costs remain closely watched. As detailed by Aviation Week and Emirates' 2025–26 annual financial results, Clark recently pointed to the A380 as the most profitable asset in Emirates' fleet during its record financial year. Broad demand for premium and main cabins helped support those results.
body_zh: 航空公司和机场管理毕业生、商业飞行员学生和商业航空作家。

空客 A380 每小时燃烧的燃油远超过 3,000 加仑（约 11,356 升），明显高于现代宽体飞机的预期。尽管数字很高，阿联酋航空仍将这架四引擎超级客机作为其长途网络的核心。在更广泛的航空业中，大多数航空公司都缩减、停放或退役了双层飞机，因为四台发动机在普通航线上带来了急剧的燃油消耗和繁重的维护需求。阿联酋航空不顾这一趋势，继续在全球主要干线航线上使用飞机，将每小时的高消耗量作为其商业战略的核心要素。
当其他航空公司将其视为商业责任时，每小时消耗数千加仑的机身如何还能获得回报？成功最终来自于在航班时刻有限的机场中填满数百个座位，并以强大的连接枢纽客流量为后盾。仔细观察 A380 的燃油消耗、每座经济性、枢纽优势、财务记录和未来前景，很明显该类型对于阿联酋航空来说仍然有意义。

以每小时计算，A380 的燃油消耗在现代双引擎长途飞机中脱颖而出。 Simple Flying 引用的数据显示，A380 的燃油消耗约为每小时 4,600 加仑（约 17,413 升），几乎是空客 A350-1000 每小时约 2,700 加仑（约 10,221 升）的两倍。这种巨大的差距源于四架大型涡轮风扇发动机将较重的双层机身移动到较长的航段，在这些航段中，起飞重量、巡航高度、逆风和航线长度不断影响着每小时的精确消耗。
正如航空公司评级所指出的那样，阿联酋航空总裁蒂姆·克拉克（Tim Clark）用重量和体积来衡量每小时的燃油消耗。克拉克表示，在从迪拜国际机场 (DXB) 飞往洛杉矶国际机场 (LAX) 的长途航班上，载有 515 名乘客，每小时燃油消耗约 13 吨（约 28,660 磅）。在两个枢纽之间的整个行程中，总燃油消耗达到约 200 吨（约 440,925 磅）。
这些数字说明了为什么当航空公司单独评估原始燃油消耗而不是总座位容量时，A380 看起来令人生畏。每小时燃烧这么多燃油会产生大量的纸面燃油费用，这自然会导致大多数航空公司寻找其他宽体机运力。考虑到这一点，在所有竞争对手都屈服于高昂成本的情况下，阿联酋航空仍坚持使用 A380 似乎有些荒谬。

Once fuel burn is divided across hundreds of seats, not just being viewed purely per hour, the A380's commercial math changes sharply.阿联酋航空总裁蒂姆·克拉克（Tim Clark）利用 AirlineRatings 所指出的迪拜与洛杉矶的比较，解释说 A380 的每个座位燃油成本可以超过运行两架波音 787 航班，而每架航班的燃油消耗大约是超级客机的一半。当高载客率使客舱充满时，这一优势仍然存在，而乘坐带有数十个空座位的大型双层飞机很快就会破坏每位乘客的效率。
起降时刻有限的机场将大量座位数转变为干线航线上更大的实用资产。据《经济学人》报道，伦敦希思罗机场 (LHR) 和香港 (HKG) 等拥挤的枢纽机场跑道和航站楼时刻稀缺，限制了航空公司起降的频率。将一架 787 投入希思罗机场一个可供 517 个座位的 A380 运行的航班上，会导致需求高峰时可供出售的座位大大减少，这对于阿联酋航空来说是不可接受的。
阿联酋航空通过其位于迪拜的转机枢纽强化了这些时刻经济，该枢纽将来自各大洲的转机乘客吸引到大容量的长途航班上。其他主要机场都专注于航线两端点对点的本地需求，而迪拜则将交通流量集中到大型客舱中，因此座位占用率始终保持在较高水平。主要目的地的稀缺时刻和迪拜稳定的转机流量共同为阿联酋航空提供了实现高座位数回报所需的乘客量。
很少有其他航空公司拥有与阿联酋航空如此一致地运营 A380 的网络规模、起降时刻压力和枢纽地理位置的精确组合。 Simple Flying 的报道强调，阿联酋航空的整个长途模式是围绕将通过迪拜的全球转接交通输送到高容量的干线航线上来构建的。许多其他航空公司更严重地依赖当地的点对点需求，或者在分散的二级市场上分散飞行，而在这些市场上，每天填满 500 个座位是很难持续做到的。
枢纽结构和时刻组合的差异也解释了为什么竞争对手的运营商经常对双层巴士得出不同的结论。虽然一些航空公司在目的地面临着严格的跑道限制，但它们可能缺乏具有相同全球覆盖范围或机队集中度的中央连接枢纽，无法在各个季节保持大型客舱满员。当需求下降或季节性波动袭来时，携带数百个空座位对运营利润率的影响远比运营小型双通道喷气式飞机严重得多。
这些结构上的对比有助于解释为什么几家航空公司比阿联酋航空更早停放或退役 A380 飞机，以及为什么其他航空公司没有将 A380 成为其机队的焦点。以法航为例：该航空公司于 2020 年退役了所有 A380 飞机，主要是因为它无法像阿联酋航空那样填补座位。如果没有阿联酋航空将转机规模和大容量干线需求结合起来的具体组合，复制其 A380 模式对于大多数航空公司来说仍然是遥不可及的。
A380 在阿联酋航空的商业案例得到了多年财务业绩的支持，而不仅仅是理论上的座位数学。在疫情爆发之前，阿联酋航空总裁蒂姆·克拉克 (Tim Clark) 告诉 Simple Flying，阿联酋航空约 85% 的利润来自 A380，因为双层客机始终保持客满状态，并且对每个客舱都产生了强劲的需求。头等舱、商务舱和经济舱的高入住率将大量乘客数量转化为长途干线的可观收入。
尽管燃油费用和运营成本仍受到密切关注，但阿联酋航空的利润贡献仍创下了现代纪录。正如《航空周刊》和阿联酋航空 2025-26 年度财务业绩所详述的那样，克拉克最近指出，在创纪录的财政年度中，A380 是阿联酋航空机队中最赚钱的资产。对高级客舱和主客舱的广泛需求支撑了这些业绩。

title_en: How Much Does A Rolls-Royce Trent 1000 Engine Cost?
title_zh: 劳斯莱斯遄达 1000 发动机的成本是多少？
summary: Estimates put a Trent 1000 near $20 million, but shop visits and the new XE upgrade shape what it really costs to own.
summary_zh: 据估计，一辆 Trent 1000 接近 2000 万美元，但商店参观和新的 XE 升级决定了它的实际拥有成本。
body_en: Jack comes to Simple Flying with a lifelong interest in all things aviation. He holds a degree in Aerospace Engineering from Georgia Tech, and is a certified private and remote pilot. Beyond these experiences, Jack previously worked for a corporate flight department where he gained first-hand experience in the world of business aviation. Currently, Jack works in the professional services industry and continues to build his flight hours outside of work.

Rolls-Royce does not publish list prices for the Trent 1000 , so every figure quoted for the Dreamliner engine is an estimate, and the most commonly cited is about $20 million per engine. That number answers only part of the question, because transaction prices differ from list estimates and the expense that has defined this engine’s reputation arrives years after delivery in the form of shop visits and retrofit campaigns.

A better answer therefore separates three prices: what an engine is estimated to cost at list, what a documented order implies once its fine print is read, and what it costs to keep one flying. This article works through each, then examines how Rolls-Royce’s latest upgrade could change the ownership economics.

Simple Flying’s 2025 survey of commercial engines places the Trent 1000 at an estimated $20 million, which sits below the roughly $22 million it assigns to the rival GE GEnx and well below Rolls-Royce’s own Trent 7000 at $25 million and Trent XWB at $35 million. The Trent 1000 can reach 74,411 pounds of thrust (331 kN), and the Trent 7000’s thrust band falls within that limit as well, so thrust alone does not explain the price spread. SlashGear arrives at the same $20 million figure and describes an engine optimized for the Boeing 787, with a fan that produces about 85% of the engine’s total thrust.

These figures are best read as list-price approximations rather than transaction prices, since common estimates exclude discounts, bulk purchase pricing, and support contracts. For example, Singapore Airlines had an order for 62 GE9X engines with a list value of about $45 million per engine, including a 12-year service contract. For context, narrowbody engines are not necessarily cheaper once transactions replace estimates: Willis Lease Finance purchased 15 Pratt & Whitney PW1100 engines in 2024 for $363.9 million, about $24.3 million each, more than the Trent 1000 estimate.

The clearest official data point is a January 2018 announcement in which Rolls-Royce said lessor AerCap had ordered Trent 1000 engines to power 10 Boeing 787s, a deal valued at $450 million at list prices. Dividing by 20 engines yields $22.5 million apiece, the figure usually quoted, but the arithmetic depends on assumptions the announcement does not confirm: two engines per aircraft and no spares.

A footnote in the release adds a more significant caveat, since Rolls-Royce measures its order book at list prices and, for long-term aftermarket contracts, counts the revenue it expects to recognize within seven years of the announcement. The release does not say whether such revenue sits inside the $450 million, so the $22.5 million figure may blend hardware with service value and should be treated as an upper reference for the engine itself rather than a price tag. The footnote also cautions that an order’s stated value may not reflect future revenue.

Two other details bound the interpretation, since the order covered the TEN variant, which entered service in November 2017, and AerCap held options on five more aircraft outside the stated value. The TEN draws on Trent XWB and Advance technologies and helps the Dreamliner achieve 20% greater efficiency than the aircraft it replaces, according to Rolls-Royce. Rolls-Royce also notes that the Trent 1000 powered the first flight of every Dreamliner version, the 787-8, 787-9, and 787-10. Because list prices exclude negotiated discounts, the price AerCap actually paid is not disclosed in the announcement.
Ownership Costs: Shop Visits And Service Contracts

Purchase price is only the entry fee, because Simple Flying reports that a single unscheduled shop visit can exceed $5 million once transport logistics, spare engine leasing, and teardown labor are counted. The same report says early Trent 1000s achieved time-on-wing intervals that were a fraction of the GEnx-1B benchmark of more than 20,000 operating hours before the first major shop visit, which made the interval the main driver of lifetime cost. Because the Trent 1000 is a three-shaft design built exclusively for the Dreamliner, its tooling, spare parts, and overhaul procedures are unique to it and are not shared with the GEnx fleet.

Many Rolls-Royce operators shield themselves from that volatility through TotalCare, a power-by-the-hour agreement in which the airline pays a fixed rate per flight hour and the manufacturer assumes the cost of shop visits. Such contracts convert an uncertain maintenance expense into a predictable one, though the engine’s true cost to the operator then becomes a recurring rate rather than a single purchase price. Because the fleet now spans several build standards, airlines and maintenance hubs must also manage parts inventories and tooling for each sub-generation, an overhead that TotalCare terms do not remove.

Rolls-Royce’s exposure under those agreements explains why durability failures hurt it directly: in 2019, the company said added repair costs would push a small number of its contracts into loss-making territory, which its finance chief put at around three. Those losses made up about half of an exceptional charge of about £1.4 billion expected that year.

The technical cause was corrosion-related fatigue cracking in the intermediate- and high-pressure turbine blades, which emerged within five years of the engine’s 2011 entry into service and eventually affected as many as 500 engines. Groundings peaked at close to 50 Dreamliners in 2018, and in April of that year the FAA cut extended-range twin-engine operating time for Package C aircraft from 330 minutes to 140, a restriction that complicated long trans-Pacific planning. Operators such as Air New Zealand and British Airways grounded aircraft for inspections, and several affected carriers leased older, less fuel-efficient jets to protect schedules, which added millions of dollars in operating expense.

The financial tally has grown with each update: by November 2019, Rolls-Royce put the cost of the Trent 1000 problems at £2.4 billion for 2017 through 2023, an additional £800 million, and said the TEN would need servicing every four years instead of five. Later accounts place the total above $3 billion, covering retrofits, engine modifications, and customer compensation.
body_zh: Jack 带着对航空一切事物的终生兴趣加入了 Simple Flying。他拥有佐治亚理工学院的航空航天工程学位，并且是一名经过认证的私人和远程飞行员。除了这些经验之外，杰克还曾在公司飞行部门工作过，在那里他获得了公务航空领域的第一手经验。目前，杰克在专业服务行业工作，并在工作之外继续增加飞行时间。
劳斯莱斯没有公布遄达 1000 的标价，因此梦想客机发动机的每一个报价都是估算值，最常见的报价是每台发动机约 2000 万美元。这个数字只能回答部分问题，因为交易价格与清单上的估计不同，而且决定该发动机声誉的费用是在交付数年后以商店访问和改造活动的形式出现的。
因此，更好的答案是区分三个价格：一台发动机的预计成本是多少，一旦阅读了其细则，所记录的订单意味着什么，以及维持一台发动机的飞行成本是多少。本文将逐一介绍，然后探讨劳斯莱斯的最新升级将如何改变所有权经济学。

Simple Flying 对 2025 年商用发动机的调查显示，Trent 1000 的售价估计为 2000 万美元，低于其竞争对手 GE GEnx 的约 2200 万美元，也远低于劳斯莱斯自己的 Trent 7000 的 2500 万美元和 Trent XWB 的 3500 万美元。 Trent 1000 的推力可以达到 74,411 磅（331 kN），而 Trent 7000 的推力范围也在该限制之内，因此推力本身并不能解释价格差异。 SlashGear 也给出了同样的 2000 万美元数字，并描述了一款针对波音 787 进行优化的发动机，其风扇可产生发动机总推力的 85% 左右。

这些数字最好理解为目录价格近似值，而不是交易价格，因为常见的估计不包括折扣、批量采购定价和支持合同。例如，新加坡航空订购了 62 台 GE9X 发动机，每台发动机的标价约为 4500 万美元，其中包括 12 年的服务合同。就背景而言，一旦交易取代预估，窄体发动机不一定更便宜：Willis Lease Finance 在 2024 年以 3.639 亿美元购买了 15 台普惠 PW1100 发动机，每台约 2430 万美元，高于 Trent 1000 的预估。
最清晰的官方数据是 2018 年 1 月的一份公告，其中劳斯莱斯表示，出租人 AerCap 已订购 Trent 1000 发动机，为 10 架波音 787 提供动力，这笔交易按标价计算价值 4.5 亿美元。通常引用的数字是，除以 20 台发动机，每台发动机为 2250 万美元，但计算结果取决于公告未证实的假设：每架飞机配备两台发动机，没有备件。
新闻稿中的脚注增加了一个更重要的警告，因为劳斯莱斯以标价衡量其订单簿，并且对于长期售后市场合同，计算其预计在公告后七年内确认的收入。该新闻稿并未说明此类收入是否包含在 4.5 亿美元之内，因此 2250 万美元的数字可能将硬件与服务价值结合在一起，应将其视为引擎本身的上限参考，而不是价格标签。脚注还警告说，订单的标明价值可能无法反映未来的收入。

另外两个细节限制了解释，因为该订单涵盖了 TEN 型号，该型号于 2017 年 11 月投入使用，并且 AerCap 持有超出规定价值的另外五架飞机的选择权。罗尔斯·罗伊斯表示，TEN 借鉴了遄达 XWB 和 Advance 技术，帮助梦想飞机实现比其取代的飞机高 20% 的效率。劳斯莱斯还指出，遄达 1000 为梦想客机各版本 787-8、787-9 和 787-10 的首飞提供了动力。由于标价不包括协商折扣，因此 AerCap 实际支付的价格并未在公告中披露。
拥有成本：商店访问和服务合同

购买价格只是入场费，因为 Simple Flying 报告称，如果算上运输物流、备用发动机租赁和拆卸人工，单次计划外的商店参观可能会超过 500 万美元。同一份报告称，早期 Trent 1000 实现的在翼时间间隔只是 GEnx-1B 基准（在首次大型车间访问之前超过 20,000 个运行小时）的一小部分，这使得该间隔成为生命周期成本的主要驱动因素。由于 Trent 1000 是专为梦想客机打造的三轴设计，因此其工具、备件和大修程序都是其独有的，不与 GEnx 机队共享。

许多劳斯莱斯运营商通过TotalCare保护自己免受这种波动的影响，TotalCare是一种按小时收费的协议，其中航空公司按飞行小时支付固定费率，制造商承担商店访问的费用。此类合同将不确定的维护费用转化为可预测的维护费用，尽管发动机对运营商的真实成本随后变成了经常性费用而不是单一购买价格。由于机队现在跨越多种建造标准，航空公司和维护中心还必须管理每个子代的零件库存和工具，这是 TotalCare 条款无法消除的开销。
劳斯莱斯在这些协议下所面临的风险解释了为什么耐用性故障会直接损害它：2019年，该公司表示，增加的维修成本将使其少数合同陷入亏损，其财务负责人预计亏损额约为三份。这些损失约占当年预计的约 14 亿英镑特殊费用的一半。

技术原因是中压和高压涡轮叶片中与腐蚀相关的疲劳裂纹，该裂纹在发动机 2011 年投入使用后的五年内出现，最终影响了多达 500 台发动机。 2018 年，停飞高峰期有近 50 架梦想飞机，同年 4 月，美国联邦航空局 (FAA) 将 C 包飞机的增程双引擎运行时间从 330 分钟缩短至 140 分钟，这一限制使长期的跨太平洋计划变得复杂。新西兰航空和英国航空等运营商停飞了飞机进行检查，几家受影响的运营商租用了较旧、燃油效率较低的飞机来保证航班时刻表，这增加了数百万美元的运营费用。
财务数字随着每次更新而增长：到 2019 年 11 月，劳斯莱斯将 2017 年至 2023 年特伦特 1000 问题的成本定为 24 亿英镑，额外增加 8 亿英镑，并表示 10 需要每四年而不是五年进行一次维修。后来的账目显示总额超过 30 亿美元，涵盖改装、发动机改造和客户赔偿。

title_en: Lawmakers Criticize FAA Deploying New “Untested” AI Tool Days Before Nationwide Grounding
title_zh: 立法者批评美国联邦航空局在全国停飞前几天部署新的“未经测试”的人工智能工具
summary: Lawmakers have questioned the FAA's accelerated nationwide AI rollout amid mounting concerns over air traffic control safety and modernization.
summary_zh: 由于人们对空中交通管制安全和现代化的担忧日益加剧，立法者对美国联邦航空局加速在全国范围内推广人工智能的做法提出了质疑。
body_en: Paul has had a career of 25+ years focused on the international technology sector, which has taken him to over 100 countries. Along the way, he developed a deep love for aviation, with a travel bucket list measured by aircraft types flown rather than destinations reached. Now he brings that avgeek passion, along with the journalism experience he accumulated early in his career, to write insightful pieces for Simple Flying.

A group of 24 Democratic lawmakers has criticized the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) for prematurely deploying a new artificial intelligence (AI) tool across US airspace. In a letter to FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford on Tuesday, the lawmakers accused the agency of expanding a largely untested system nationwide before completing its promised 90-day validation period.

The nationwide deployment of the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories (SMART) system came just three days before a telecommunications failure brought US departures to a standstill . While the FAA has denied any connection between the two events, the controversy raises fresh questions about whether the Trump administration's ambitious air traffic control (ATC) modernization program is prioritizing the speed of implementation over adequate testing, safety oversight, and transparency.

Led by House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee Ranking Member Rick Larsen, the lawmakers allege that the FAA expanded the SMART system nationwide without notifying Congress in advance. The expansion came just 50 days after its initial deployment in the Washington area , despite the FAA previously outlining a 90-day validation period.
In their letter to Bedford, the lawmakers expressed frustration with the lack of supporting safety data.
“We have yet to receive any substantive information proving the system was properly validated before its nationwide expansion.”

Concerns surrounding SMART considerably predate the nationwide grounding. In September, the National Air Traffic Controllers Association (NATCA) told Flying Magazine that it had been excluded from the system's development, testing, and implementation. Lawmakers subsequently requested that the FAA suspend SMART operations and called for an independent Government Accountability Office (GAO) audit. More troublingly, the latest letter cites allegations that FAA employees who raised safety concerns about SMART's accelerated deployment may have faced retaliation.
SMART launches at three Washington-area airports
NATCA's exclusion from development and testing is reported
Lawmakers request suspension of SMART operations
Congressional request for an independent GAO audit
SMART expands to all 22 enroute control centers
FAA and DOT officials scheduled to testify before Congress

The lawmakers have presented the FAA with 13 questions, demanding details on its safety assessments, performance metrics, controller training, cybersecurity protections, and contingency plans if SMART experiences an outage. They also question why the agency prioritized deploying SMART over essential infrastructure upgrades, including radar replacements. Reuters reported that the FAA has declined to address the allegations publicly, saying it will respond directly to lawmakers.

Developed by Air Space Intelligence (ASI) under an $875 million, 12-year contract, SMART is designed to make the increasingly congested US airspace more efficient. The cloud-based technology consolidates approximately 200 data streams, encompassing weather forecasts, flight trajectories, airport capacity, and controller staffing. Its predictive capabilities allow aviation professionals to anticipate operational bottlenecks and identify alternative flight paths before disruptions materialize.

Importantly, SMART does not autonomously direct aircraft. FAA specialists at a dedicated center in Washington review its recommendations before forwarding them to the agency's Air Traffic Control System Command Center in Warrenton, Virginia. Human controllers retain ultimate operational authority. The technology is similar to ASI's Flyways AI platform, which Alaska Airlines began using in 2021 to help flight dispatchers optimize aircraft routing.

The potential commercial benefits are substantial, and United Airlines, Delta Air Lines, American Airlines, and Southwest Airlines have all expressed support for the initiative. According to the FAA, and as reported by Aerotime , SMART's initial deployment delivered measurable efficiency improvements, potentially translating into considerable fuel savings and fewer passenger disruptions when replicated nationally. However, lawmakers argue that evidence of improved operational efficiency cannot substitute for comprehensive safety validation.
Nationwide Grounding Exposes Challenges Of FAA Modernization

The concerns come amid the shock of the November 13 nationwide ground stop, which demonstrated the vulnerability of America's existing ATC infrastructure. The FAA's preliminary investigation identified a telecommunications failure, with excessive data traffic overwhelming legacy equipment following routine maintenance work. The resulting instability affected communications and radar feeds across much of the country. Both the FAA and ASI have explicitly denied that SMART contributed to the disruption.

The incident was the first nationwide ground stop since the January 2023 failure of the FAA's NOTAM system . A September 2026 GAO report highlighted significant shortcomings in the FAA's modernization cost estimates and scheduling. Previous research found that 105 of the agency's 138 ATC systems were either unsustainable or potentially unsustainable, illustrating the urgency of replacing aging infrastructure while maintaining the integrity of existing operations.
body_zh: Paul 拥有超过 25 年的职业生涯，专注于国际技术领域，足迹遍及 100 多个国家。一路走来，他对航空产生了深深的热爱，他的旅行愿望清单是根据飞行的飞机类型而不是到达的目的地来衡量的。现在，他带着这种平均极客的热情，以及他在职业生涯早期积累的新闻经验，为《简单飞行》撰写了富有洞察力的文章。
由 24 名民主党议员组成的团体批评美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 过早地在美国领空部署新的人工智能 (AI) 工具。在周二致美国联邦航空管理局局长布莱恩·贝德福德的一封信中，议员们指责该机构在完成承诺的 90 天验证期之前，在全国范围内扩展了一个基本上未经测试的系统。
空域、航线和轨迹战略管理（SMART）系统在全国范围内部署，就在三天前，一场电信故障导致美国的航班起飞陷入停滞。尽管美国联邦航空局否认这两起事件之间有任何联系，但这场争议引发了新的问题：特朗普政府雄心勃勃的空中交通管制（ATC）现代化计划是否优先考虑实施速度，而不是充分的测试、安全监督和透明度。
由众议院交通和基础设施委员会高级成员 Rick Larsen 领导的立法者声称，FAA 在没有提前通知国会的情况下在全国范围内扩展了 SMART 系统。尽管 FAA 此前规定了 90 天的验证期，但在华盛顿地区首次部署后仅 50 天就进行了扩展。
在写给贝德福德的信中，议员们对缺乏支持性安全数据表示失望。
“我们尚未收到任何实质性信息，证明该系统在全国推广之前得到了适当的验证。”
围绕 SMART 的担忧早在全国范围内停飞之前就已存在。 9 月，美国国家空中交通管制员协会 (NATCA) 告诉《飞行杂志》，它已被排除在该系统的开发、测试和实施之外。立法者随后要求美国联邦航空局暂停 SMART 运营，并要求进行独立的政府问责办公室 (GAO) 审计。更令人不安的是，最新的信函援引指控称，对 SMART 加速部署提出安全担忧的 FAA 员工可能面临报复。
SMART 在华盛顿地区的三个机场推出
据报道 NATCA 被排除在开发和测试之外
立法者要求暂停 SMART 运营
国会要求政府问责局进行独立审计
SMART 扩展到所有 22 个航路控制中心
美国联邦航空局和交通部官员计划在国会作证
立法者向 FAA 提出了 13 个问题，要求提供有关其安全评估、性能指标、控制器培训、网络安全保护以及 SMART 发生故障时的应急计划的详细信息。他们还质疑为什么该机构优先考虑部署 SMART，而不是重要的基础设施升级，包括雷达更换。路透社报道称，美国联邦航空局拒绝公开回应这些指控，称将直接向立法者做出回应。
SMART 由航空航天情报局 (ASI) 根据价值 8.75 亿美元、为期 12 年的合同开发，旨在提高日益拥挤的美国空域的效率。基于云的技术整合了大约 200 个数据流，包括天气预报、飞行轨迹、机场容量和管制员人员配置。其预测能力使航空专业人士能够预测运营瓶颈，并在中断发生之前确定替代飞行路径。
重要的是，SMART 不能自主引导飞机。美国联邦航空局的专家在华盛顿的一个专门中心审查其建议，然后将其转发给该机构位于弗吉尼亚州沃伦顿的空中交通管制系统指挥中心。人类控制者保留最终的操作权力。该技术类似于 ASI 的 Flyways AI 平台，阿拉斯加航空公司于 2021 年开始使用该平台来帮助航班调度员优化飞机航线。
潜在的商业利益是巨大的，美国联合航空、达美航空、美国航空和西南航空均表示支持该举措。根据 FAA 和 Aerotime 的报道，SMART 的初始部署带来了显着的效率提升，在全国推广时可能会转化为可观的燃油节省和更少的乘客干扰。然而，立法者认为，运营效率提高的证据不能替代全面的安全验证。
全国停飞暴露了美国联邦航空局现代化的挑战
这些担忧是在 11 月 13 日全国范围内的地面停车事件令人震惊的背景下产生的，这表明了美国现有 ATC 基础设施的脆弱性。美国联邦航空局的初步调查发现存在电信故障，在进行例行维护工作后，过多的数据流量淹没了遗留设备。由此产生的不稳定影响了全国大部分地区的通信和雷达信号。 FAA 和 ASI 均明确否认 SMART 造成了此次干扰。
该事件是自 2023 年 1 月 FAA NOTAM 系统故障以来首次全国范围内的地面停车事件。 GAO 2026 年 9 月的一份报告强调了 FAA 现代化成本估算和调度方面的重大缺陷。此前的研究发现，该机构的 138 个 ATC 系统中有 105 个要么不可持续，要么可能不可持续，这说明更换老化基础设施同时保持现有运营完整性的紧迫性。

title_en: The Real Reason Why Boeing Never Believed In Gear Doors For Its Best-Selling Jet
title_zh: 波音公司从不相信其最畅销的喷气式飞机配备起落架舱门的真正原因
summary: A closer look at the advantages of sticking with exposed landing gear bays for the 737.
